attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack essay. The works he cites are offered as examples, but the claim itself is his.

semantics.note: Keeps 'over the last couple years' and 'steadily'. This is a firm retrospective observation.

contract.note: Reading 'public credibility' as perceived trustworthiness and 'steadily' as a sustained decline is the ordinary meaning. Asking for repeated comparable measures is demanding, but it fits a trend claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet contains no evidence items. The sources considered were snapshots of popularity or favorability, or measured OpenAI's reputation; none was a repeated measure of Altman's credibility. Nothing shows the decline or a steady trend over 2024–2026, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own essay.

semantics.note: Faithful to the statement. 'Caught up' is relative to OpenAI, which the context implies.

contract.note: Reading 'caught up' as being in the same capability tier, not exact parity, is an ordinary and fair reading. The window of Q4 2025 to publication was the evaluator's choice and is reasonable.

evidence.note: Nov 2025 index: Gemini 3 Pro 73, Claude Opus 4.5 70, GPT-5.1 70, Kimi 67, Grok 4 65. Anthropic and Google are level with OpenAI, and xAI and Moonshot are close behind.
Nov 2025: Kimi K2 Thinking at 67, second only to GPT-5 among proprietary models, and ahead of MiniMax-M2 and DeepSeek. Shows Chinese labs are close.

Year-end retrospective, published Feb 2026 (before the evaluation date). It calls the frontier fiercely contested between OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, with Chinese labs rising. OpenAI keeps a narrow lead, which fits tier parity rather than exact equality.

reviews.rationale: Independent multi-task index results from late 2025 place Anthropic and Google level with OpenAI. xAI and several Chinese labs (Moonshot, MiniMax, DeepSeek) are within a few points. OpenAI's narrow year-end lead does not undercut 'caught up' in the ordinary sense. One caveat: all three items come from a single benchmarking organization.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own essay.

semantics.note: Keeps both parts: price wars happened, and costs per token fell roughly 100x over about two years.

contract.note: Comparing API prices at matched capability is a fair ordinary reading of 'costs per token'. Marcus named no model basket, so the choice of basis could change the result.

evidence.note: Reuters, May 2024: Alibaba, Baidu and ByteDance made competitive LLM price cuts. Supports the price-war part only.
Epoch, Mar 2025: fitted annual declines of 9x to 900x depending on the milestone. This is not a measured Jan 2024 to Jan 2026 ratio.

reviews.rationale: The price-war part is supported by e1. The packet has no capability-matched comparison of the two endpoints, so the central ~100x figure over two years is neither confirmed nor contradicted. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is fully met.

attribution.note: Marcus's own characterization in his own essay.

semantics.note: The factual core is kept. The evaluative words ('atrocious', 'unconvincing') are rightly left out of scoring.

contract.note: The result depends on reading 'couldn't begin to explain' as 'gave no identifiable mechanism', as opposed to 'gave nothing convincing'. That literal reading of firm wording is fair, and persuasiveness is set aside.

evidence.note: Fortune report from the same week: in the BG2 exchange, Altman named steep revenue growth from ChatGPT, an AI cloud business, devices and science. It is a high-level mechanism without a cash-flow reconciliation.

reviews.rationale: A reliable report of the exchange shows Altman did name ways OpenAI expected to generate revenue to cover its commitments. That counts as beginning an explanation, however thin. Whether the answer was convincing is opinion and is not scored. The literal claim that he couldn't begin to explain is contradicted.
